strengths: Comprehensive full-stack solution addressing real bottleneck in open-source MLLM development with clear motivation and positioning
Strong empirical results with Bee-8B achieving SOTA among fully open models and competitive performance with semi-open alternatives on most benchmarks
Excellent ablation studies clearly demonstrating impact of noise filtering and CoT enrichment with 15-20% gains on reasoning tasks
Transparent and reproducible methodology including detailed pipeline descriptions, complete prompts, qualitative examples, and commitment to releasing resources
Thorough evaluation across 30+ benchmarks with comprehensive stage-by-stage analysis demonstrating cumulative training benefits
Well-designed case studies illustrating data quality issues and enrichment examples across diverse domains
Practical value to open-source community through combination of high-quality dataset, reusable pipeline framework, and trained model
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty—relies on established techniques (data filtering, CoT enrichment, LLM-as-judge) without introducing fundamentally new methods
Contradicts 'fully open' positioning by relying on proprietary models (GPT-4-level, Qwen2.5-VL-72B) for data generation; computational costs undisclosed, limiting reproducibility
Insufficient rigorous analysis of data quality—no systematic quality metrics, inter-rater agreement studies, or validation of automated fidelity verification against human judgment
CoT design choices lack justification: no sensitivity analysis for 12.2M/2.7M split, and routing mechanism may introduce subtle biases
Evaluation concerns: mix of metrics and reliance on LLM-as-judge (known to be problematic); customized VLMEvalKit modifications underspecified
Missing critical analyses including benchmark contamination assessment, failure case characterization, and computational cost-benefit analysis
Comparison fairness questionable—semi-open baselines use different LLMs and training procedures; missing ablation with Bee-8B trained on alternative high-quality datasets
Clarity gaps in DataStudio framework: unclear how modular and adaptable it is for new domains; limited examples of alternative instantiations

strengths: Significant practical contribution addressing real performance gaps in open MLLMs through principled data quality focus
Comprehensive resource release (dataset, pipeline, model, training recipes) with exceptional reproducibility documentation including data contamination analysis and inter-model agreement studies
Thorough experimental evaluation across 29 diverse benchmarks with solid empirical results competitive with semi-open models and well-designed ablation studies
Well-engineered dual-level CoT enrichment strategy (short/long CoT) that is intuitive, scalable, and effectively addresses the complex reasoning gap in open datasets
Transparent data curation pipeline architecture that moves beyond static dataset releases toward reproducible, modular methodologies
Extensive validation including human evaluation, cross-model evaluation robustness, stability analysis across 5 runs, and detailed noise case studies
weaknesses: Misleading 'fully open' claims: data curation critically depends on proprietary models (Qwen2.5-VL-72B, GPT-4) for filtering and long CoT generation, blocking reproduction by most researchers without proprietary API access
No cost analysis provided for API-based data curation at 15M scale, making practical reproducibility and adoption unclear for the research community
Limited methodological novelty: individual components (rule-based filtering, LLM-as-Judge verification, CoT enrichment) are established techniques; contribution is primarily engineering-focused
Incomplete trade-off analysis: fidelity verification prioritizes precision over recall, but cost of discarded valid data is not quantified or explored
Small-scale human evaluation (532 comparisons on 38 questions) with high tie rate (83.65%) suggests conservative verification; no systematic error analysis of remaining dataset quality issues

Evaluation methodology concerns: primary use of Qwen3-32B judge introduces potential bias toward Qwen-based models; notable cross-judge differences (2-3.6%) on some benchmarks highlight evaluation subjectivity
Dataset distribution heavily skewed toward General (36.8%) and Chart (24.6%) domains with limited exploration of generalization to underrepresented domains
Limited novelty in architecture and marginal performance improvements: Bee-8B uses standard design; gains over LLaVA-OneVision are solid (5-10 points) but not breakthrough
Missing key analyses: no per-source contribution metrics, no data efficiency analysis, limited failure case discussion, no exploration of alternative verification strategies
Reproducibility gaps despite extensive documentation: some implementation details missing, pipeline requires proprietary APIs, cost and feasibility for other labs unclear
